summary: Updates RFC 3326 so a SIP message can carry multiple Reason header field values for the same protocol, when that protocol defines what multiple values mean. The original rule allowed only one value per protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo updates the SIP Reason header rule so a message can include multiple values for one protocol when that protocol explains how to interpret them. Otherwise, the message must still include only one value per protocol.

what does rfc 9366 change in rfc 3326
subtitle: Allows multiple SIP Reason values for a protocol when that protocol defines their meaning.

tldr.problem: RFC 3326 allowed only one Reason value per protocol, although some registered protocols can define useful meanings for multiple values.
tldr.mechanism: The update permits multiple values for a protocol only when that registered protocol defines what multiple values mean.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9366 updates RFC 3326 and retains the one-value limit for protocols without such a definition.

today: RFC 9366 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 3326. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 9366.

sections.title: Why Multiple Reason Values Are Useful
sections.content: The SIP Reason header field in RFC 3326 allows only one Reason value for each protocol value. Experience with newer protocols showed that multiple values for the same protocol can be useful. RFC 9366 updates the rule only for registered protocols that define what multiple values mean.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier rule allowed one reason for each protocol. This update allows several when that protocol defines how to read them.

sections.title: The Updated Rule
sections.content: A SIP message MAY contain more than one Reason value. If the registered protocol for a value specifies what multiple values mean in one message, more than one value for that protocol MAY be present. Otherwise, there MUST be only one value per protocol, such as one SIP value and one Q.850 value. Implementations remain free to ignore Reason values they do not understand.
sections.plainLanguage: A message may contain several reasons for one protocol if that protocol defines their meaning. If it does not, the message must use only one value for that protocol.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content: The RFC adds no security considerations to SIP. Readers should consider the security guidance in RFC 3326 and in any registered protocols used in Reason values. This document has no IANA actions.
sections.plainLanguage: The change adds no new SIP security considerations. The RFC does not require any IANA action.

references.text: Schulzrinne, H., Oran, D., and G. Camarillo, "The Reason Header Field for the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP)", RFC 3326, December 2002.
